A B S T R A C T
These days, most people can’t imagine their life without their networks. People rely more and more on networks  as new technologies like 5G and the Internet of Things proliferate, and networks are becoming larger and more  complicated by the day. Consequently, the enormous networked society is under increasing danger from cyber  attacks, which are also growing in number, sophistication, and variety. Users’ private data can end up in the  wrong hands. Data communicated via a network might be compromised in some way. It is also possible to target  the computer infrastructure that is linked to the network. Thus, NIDS is crucial in ensuring that contemporary  society’s network communication environment is secure and dependable. This work proposes a detection model  that is both lightweight and effective. This model is able to keep its high detection accuracy by combining the  benefits of SNN and CNN with logical algorithm design. On top of that, it can bring attention to clear strengths in  relation to computing efficiency and power usage. The suggested model was tested against a number of state-of-  the-art models using an extensive and integrated set of benchmarks. With a 23 % improvement in detection  accuracy (AD), a 19 % improvement in delay, and a 28 % improvement in consumption energy, the suggested  technique outperformed the Spiking DFR + MLP and Spike-DHS methods in the simulations.
1. Introduction
One of the most important components of keeping computer systems  and information networks secure is intrusion detection (Bul’ajoul et al.,  2018; Zarzoor et al., 2023). The need for innovative and effective so­ lutions in the area of security intrusion detection and prevention is  growing as a result of the advancement of information and communi­ cation technology (Ahmad et al., 2023; Laghrissi et al., 2021; Lightbody  et al., 2022). One of the most cutting-edge and effective approaches in  this area for intrusion detection is the application of convolutional  neural networks (Fomin et al., 2023; Sattari et al., 2021).
Because of their bio-inspired design, Speaking Neural Networks  (SNNs) have significant theoretical implications (Yu et al., 2021).  Compared to traditional deep neural networks, they behave more like  biological neurons (DNNs). Similar to real neurons, neurons communi­ cate by spike waveforms and function asynchronously, that is, produc­ ing output spikes before all input neurons have spiked (Yamazaki et al.,  2022). The key reason SNNs are practically promising is that they have a  tremendous potential to achieve high energy efficiency, which is crucial
for big and deep neural network applications that are used in mobile and  Internet of Things applications (Zhou et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2022). For  high-speed applications, the asynchronous working principle may lead  to minimal latency, which is appealing (Qi et al., 2022). Convolutional  neural networks have shown to be an effective tool for intrusion  detection in systems and networks because they can extract significant  features from input data and are especially well-suited for processing  images and real-world data (Zhang et al., 2023; Cao et al., 2021).
Over the past ten years, artificial neural networks (ANNs) have  developed enormously, from multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) in the first  generation to deep neural networks (DNNs) in the second. Despite this  significant progress, ANNs are still inferior to biological neural networks  in terms of energy efficiency and online learning (Sun et al., 2020).  Power consumption of traditional deep learning models has been the  target of numerous attempts to minimize it. In order to find more  compact networks with comparable performance but fewer parameters  and less complexity than the original network, many different strategies  have been devised. Despite having a neural network foundation, artificial neural net­ works (ANNs) and deep neural networks (DNNs) are fundamentally  different from biological neural networks in terms of their architecture,  neural computations, and learning principles (Li et al., 2023). The most  appropriate model for the biological neuron is the one that is utilized in  SNNs; this model is closest to the biological neuron mechanism (Li et al.,  2023). In order to facilitate event-driven calculations, the SNN uses the  pulse neurons to collect the input to the membrane voltage. Once the  threshold is achieved, the pulse is then released. Higher levels of energy  efficiency can be achieved by SNNs because of the sparse nature of pulse  events and the event-driven computing method used to process them  (Zhang et al., 2021). SNNs can handle sparsity present in biological  systems and are very compatible with temporal coding since they share  functional traits with biological neural networks (Liu et al., 2023; Zhou  et al., 2022a,b).
Researchers are actively investigating potential utilization patterns  for SNNs, despite the fact that they are not as common as DNNs in  application settings at this time (Zheng et al., 2023). SNNs are already as  accurate as DNNs in certain tasks (Zhang et al., 2023), and they usually  need a lot less energy to run.
In recent years, the use of deep learning (DL) techniques has  attracted considerable attention in the field of intrusion detection due to  their potential to detect complex patterns from large amounts of  network data. However, traditional DL models, such as convolutional  neural networks (CNN) and recurrent neural networks (RNN), are often  resource intensive and may not be suitable for environments with  limited computational resources and energy constraints. To address  these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative approach that uses  Convolutional Spiking Neural Networks (CSNN) for intrusion detection.  Unlike traditional DL models, CSNNs offer inherent advantages,  including distributed computing and temporal dynamics, which make  them suitable for real-time processing and resource-constrained envi­ ronments. While existing research has explored the potential of SNNs in  various applications, including pattern recognition and signal process­ ing, their application in intrusion detection remains relatively unknown.  By combining the strengths of SNN and CNN, the proposed model aims  to provide a lightweight yet effective solution for intrusion detection,  capable of being efficient even in environments with limited computing  resources and energy resources.
The motivation for choosing CSNN over traditional methods lies in  its ability to mimic the performance of biological neural networks and  improve accuracy and efficiency in intrusion detection, which enables  event-driven computing. By using convolutional neural networks, which  are suitable for extracting important features from complex data, the  main goal of this research is to improve the level of security in systems  and networks through the development and improvement of an intru­ sion detection model using convolutional neural networks, as well as  increasing the ability Detecting intrusive patterns in data. The main  contribution of the authors in this research is as follows:
• The data-triggered spike information is encoded using a time-value  technique. Complex spike trigger patterns can be mapped to a  uniquely determined value by employing this encoding. Without  making the model data transfer procedure more difficult, informa­ tion can be given to the processing processes in a more compre­ hensive way.   • A loss function that fits the suggested model is customized. It can  offer supervision to make sure the model approximates the correct  result in multiple dimensions, ranging from measures like the accu­ racy of the present classification to the ranking of the correct clas­ sification in the inferred results.   • A brand-new intrusion detection model architecture is put out and  put into practice, based on convolutional and spiking networks. Ex­ periments show that the model can continue to secure the target
device under difficult circumstances and can adapt more effectively  to contexts with limited resources.
This paper’s remaining sections are arranged as follows. Section 2  offers a synopsis of the relevant material. Section 3 outlines the solution  we have in mind. Section 4 examines and assesses the performance of  the models that were adopted. The experiment results are compiled in  Section 5, along with workable ideas for further study directions.
2. Related work
Spiking neural networks (SNNs) have advanced significantly in terms  of efficiency and performance over the last few years, but their devel­ opment is still trailing behind that of traditional artificial neural net­ works (ANNs) due to their peculiar working pattern, which makes it  challenging to train high-performance SNNs with low latency (Wu et al.,  2020).  Spiking Neural Networks uses computationally efficient, biologically  realistic models of neurons to bridge the gap between neuroscience and  machine learning. Spiking neural networks are extremely adaptive to  time coding and are able to capture the scatter observed in biology due  to their functional resemblance to the biological neural network. Re­ searchers have provided a thorough analysis of biological neuron hy­ potheses in (Guo et al., 2023). Additionally, they have evaluated several  spike-based neuron models that have been researched in the field of  neuroscience. After that, they discussed the spiking neural network  applications that are now being used in the fields of robotics and com­ puter vision. Finally, they evaluated the spiking neuron frameworks that  have been developed to facilitate the implementation of spiking neural  networks.
Neural networks (SNN) have garnered increasing attention in the  past few years for categorization applications. Spiking neural networks  (SNNs) are a family of neural networks that, in contrast to typical neural  networks, mimic the dynamics of biological neurons, where data is  represented as spikes or action potentials. Driven by these benefits,  scientists have suggested a method in (Xu et al., 2023) to use SNN to  identify a Wi-Fi frame and show that SNN is feasible for Wi-Fi detection.  Pre-processing to convert the gathered signals and SNN to identify Wi-Fi  frames make up this method. The usefulness of spiking neural networks  (SNN) for classifying N-BaIoT data sets is investigated in study (Zhao  et al., 2023). The spatiotemporal feature extraction capability of con­ volutional SNNs has been utilized in (Liu et al., 2023). Shallow con­ volutional SNN outperforms spatio-temporal feature extraction  techniques like C3D, ConvLstm, and Conv and Cascade LSTM, according  to the analysis that was collected. Furthermore, a novel deep architec­ ture is showcased to address practical categorization and activity  recognition assignments. Our suggested hybrid training approach is  used to train this model. In the publication (Mi et al., 2022), it was  suggested to identify intrusions using a fusion method of multi-  convolutional neural networks (multi-CNN). The feature data are split  into four sections after the correlation, and based on the one-  dimensional feature data, these sections are then transformed into  grayscale graphs. The authors (Lyu et al., 2023) presented two deep  learning-based models for classifying binary and multi-ticlass network  threats. They employ a convolutional neural network architecture to  create our models. Their models surpass comparable models in the  literature in terms of accuracy and recall, according to the results of their  studies. The study (Xuemin et al., 2023) proposes a CNN intrusion  detection algorithm based on attention.
When object detection techniques are utilized in real-time systems,  the accuracy of deep learning is decreased since it takes longer for  detected signals from IoT devices to reach the application layer. In order  to address these problems, a model-view-controller (MVC) architecture  together with a client-to-client file transfer protocol (C2CFTP) that uti­ lizes a Binarized Speaking Neural Network (BS4NN) are suggested as a  way to construct an Internet of Things smart home appliance control

The non-leaky integrate neurons fire (NLIF) model was utilized in the  SNN to choose the best input samples in order to decrease latency and  device power consumption. They take into consideration a general class  of single-spike temporal-coded integrand-fire neurons in order to study  the input–output expressions of both leaky and nonleaky neurons (Li  et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2023; Cao et al., 2023). For research to be useful,  it must be integrated into industrial processes. Even though several  studies have demonstrated the efficiency of SNNs (Tang et al., 2023;  Chen et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2023), much work remains to be done to  fully capitalize on this efficient performance. By contrast, artificial  neural networks come at a tremendous expense in terms of processing  power, memory performance, and energy consumption (Cao et al.,  2024).  With weights implemented in RRAM, the authors suggest a hybrid  SNN-CNN network to improve TSR’s computing and storage efficiency  (Xie et al., 2022). The SNN-CNN hybrid network achieves comparable  accuracy with 81.55 % less power consumption and 69.21 % less  weighted parameters when compared to the latest CNN techniques. It is suggested that quick and memory-efficient training of Activation  Consistently Coupled ANN-SNNs (AC2AS) is possible (Zhao et al., 2022).  By examining the variations between analog neurons and spiking neu­ rons, an adaptive threshold method has been developed to improve the  balance between the weight and threshold of SNNs (Xue et al., 2023).  This technique obtained state-of-the-art results on CIFAR100 and out­ performed most of the recently suggested SNNs in terms of accuracy,  accuracy loss, and network latency on CIFAR10. A Dynamic Threshold  Integrate and Fire (DTIF) model is suggested to be used, which takes use  of the differences in biological neurons’ thresholds to boost spike ac­ tivity (Cao et al., 2022). At every simulation time step, the threshold is  dynamically changed to increase spike activity and decrease latency.  The results of these investigations also shed light on potential design  approaches for energy-efficient models (Zhao et al., n.d.; Liu et al., 2022;  Chen et al., 2022).
While previous studies have explored the use of neural networks,  including CNNs, in intrusion detection, there is a gap in research  regarding the efficiency and adaptability of these models in resource-  constrained environments. This gap motivates our research on Con­ volutional Speaking Neural Networks (CSNN) as a potential solution to  the challenges faced by traditional DL models in intrusion detection.  Using the strengths of convolutional neural networks and SPEC, our  proposed approach aims to address these limitations while providing a
lightweight and efficient intrusion detection solution capable of per­ forming effectively in challenging real-world scenarios. By including a  more complete literature review, this paper provides a stronger foun­ dation for the proposed CSNN approach and emphasizes its novelty in  addressing challenges in intrusion detection.
3. Proposed scheme
This research presents a novel intrusion detection model that utilizes  convolutional spiking neural networks, which are both lightweight and  efficient. In order to optimize processing performance, it is necessary to  leverage the advantages of both spiking neural networks and convolu­ tional neural networks when developing the processing framework. The  model’s complexity has been minimized to ensure that the final version  can reliably and efficiently perform its intended function, even in  resource-constrained contexts. The overall design of the model was  achieved by striking a compromise between the requirement for  simplicity and efficiency, and the requirement for accuracy.

Following these procedures, the network traffic data will be trans­ formed into a binary matrix consisting of entries that are either 0 or 1. In order to enable organized  storage and easy visual examination, the values in each matrix elements  will be consistently scaled by a factor of 255. 4. Evaluation and simulation
The experiments included the following comparative models for  evaluation:
By combining various bio-features in various neuronal activities,  GLIF (Chen et al., 2022) is a unified spiking neuron that broadens the  representation space of spiking neurons. The gate parameters in GLIF  that control the percentage of fused bio-features can be learned during  training. This approach can produce constantly changing spiking neu­ rons that are more heterogeneous and adaptable by incorporating all  learnable membrane-related factors.
• SNN (Cao et al., 2023): Spiking Neural Network.   • Spiking DFR + MLP (Xie et al., 2022): Delayed Feedback Reservoir + Multi Layer Perceptron.   • ResNet18-GLIF (Chen et al., 2022): GLIF neurons are used by  ResNet18.   • Spike-DHS (Tang et al., 2023): This computation is spike-based and  done at both the layer and cell levels.   • MLP (Cao et al., 2024): Multi Layer Perceptron optimized.
• STDS (Wu et al., 2023): Pruning speed can be adjusted for various  stages of SNN weights by using distinct functions to characterize the  rising threshold of state transition. This section provides a comparison between the difficulty of the  suggested strategy and alternative methods. The computational diffi­ culty of detecting dynamic attacks using DFR is determined by the  computation required for the reservoirs and the updating of the readout  layer weights. equations.raw_extracted: These days, most people can’t imagine their life without their networks. People rely more and more on networks  as new technologies like 5G and the Internet of Things proliferate, and networks are becoming larger and more  complicated by the day. Consequently, the enormous networked society is under increasing danger from cyber  attacks, which are also growing in number, sophistication, and variety. Users’ private data can end up in the  wrong hands. Data communicated via a network might be compromised in some way. It is also possible to target  the computer infrastructure that is linked to the network. Thus, NIDS is crucial in ensuring that contemporary  society’s network communication environment is secure and dependable. This work proposes a detection model  that is both lightweight and effective. This model is able to keep its high detection accuracy by combining the  benefits of SNN and CNN with logical algorithm design. On top of that, it can bring attention to clear strengths in  relation to computing efficiency and power usage. The suggested model was tested against a number of state-of-  the-art models using an extensive and integrated set of benchmarks. With a 23 % improvement in detection  accuracy (AD), a 19 % improvement in delay, and a 28 % improvement in consumption energy, the suggested  technique outperformed the Spiking DFR + MLP and Spike-DHS methods in the simulations.

One of the most important components of keeping computer systems  and information networks secure is intrusion detection (Bul’ajoul et al.,  2018; Zarzoor et al., 2023). The need for innovative and effective so­ lutions in the area of security intrusion detection and prevention is  growing as a result of the advancement of information and communi­ cation technology (Ahmad et al., 2023; Laghrissi et al., 2021; Lightbody  et al., 2022). One of the most cutting-edge and effective approaches in  this area for intrusion detection is the application of convolutional  neural networks (Fomin et al., 2023; Sattari et al., 2021).

• The data-triggered spike information is encoded using a time-value  technique. Complex spike trigger patterns can be mapped to a  uniquely determined value by employing this encoding. For research to be useful,  it must be integrated into industrial processes. Even though several  studies have demonstrated the efficiency of SNNs (Tang et al., 2023;  Chen et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2023), much work remains to be done to  fully capitalize on this efficient performance. By contrast, artificial  neural networks come at a tremendous expense in terms of processing  power, memory performance, and energy consumption (Cao et al.,  2024).  With weights implemented in RRAM, the authors suggest a hybrid  SNN-CNN network to improve TSR’s computing and storage efficiency  (Xie et al., 2022). The SNN-CNN hybrid network achieves comparable  accuracy with 81.55 % less power consumption and 69.21 % less  weighted parameters when compared to the latest CNN techniques. With  the Differentiation on Spike Representation (DSR) approach, low latency  and high performance similar to ANNs can be attained (Huang et al.,  2024). The study demonstrates that DSR can deliver low latency state-of-  the-art SNN performance on both static and neuromorphic datasets. An  ultra-low-power radio frequency fingerprinting identification (RFFI)  system is constructed using SNNs (Yue et al., 2023). 64 % less power is  used by the SNN-based RFFI system than by ANNs with similar accuracy.  It is suggested that quick and memory-efficient training of Activation  Consistently Coupled ANN-SNNs (AC2AS) is possible (Zhao et al., 2022).  By examining the variations between analog neurons and spiking neu­ rons, an adaptive threshold method has been developed to improve the  balance between the weight and threshold of SNNs (Xue et al., 2023).  This technique obtained state-of-the-art results on CIFAR100 and out­ performed most of the recently suggested SNNs in terms of accuracy,  accuracy loss, and network latency on CIFAR10. A Dynamic Threshold  Integrate and Fire (DTIF) model is suggested to be used, which takes use  of the differences in biological neurons’ thresholds to boost spike ac­ tivity (Cao et al., 2022). The results of these investigations also shed light on potential design  approaches for energy-efficient models (Zhao et al., n.d.; Liu et al., 2022;  Chen et al., 2022).
